accounts.antigravity.installRequired: Checking installation. If the button stays disabled, install the agy CLI and reopen the app.
accounts.antigravity.description: OAuth 2.0 sign-in is handled by the official Antigravity CLI. It opens the browser when no saved session exists; if already connected, it reuses your account. Complete browser authentication yourself.
accounts.antigravity.scope: Mission/Fleet use this account's models, with MCP and permissions isolated per task. Use /model in the terminal to select the interactive session model.
accounts.antigravity.multipleAccounts: The CLI does not yet support simultaneous OAuth accounts: configuration profiles share the system keyring session. To switch accounts, finish active runs and use /logout, then sign in again. This changes the system account for all sessions.

settings.terminal.desc: How terminal history looks and how you move through it.
settings.terminal.zoom.desc: Makes the text in every terminal bigger or smaller. TUIs reflow to the new columns on their own.
settings.terminal.zoom.sample: This is how your agents' text looks: code, diffs and replies.
settings.terminal.marks.desc: Draws a faint line every time you send something, so one turn is visibly separated from the next when scrolling back through a long conversation.
settings.terminal.marks.limits: It keys off the Enter key, which is all the terminal can see: an Enter inside a multi-line message marks too. It does not apply to full-screen TUIs (OpenCode), where there is no scrollback to anchor the mark to.
settings.terminal.marks.applies: Applies to terminals you open from now on; already-open ones are unchanged.
settings.title: Settings
settings.appearance.desc: Switch between light and dark theme
settings.tuis.desc: Add tools not detected automatically (e.g. aider, continue, opencode)
settings.tuis.path.shellOk: On startup the app asked your shell ({{shell}}) for its PATH and added {{count}} folders it was missing.
settings.tuis.path.shellFailed: On startup the app couldn't ask your shell ({{shell}}) for its PATH: {{error}}. It searches what it inherited plus the folders TUIs install into.
settings.tuis.path.windows: On Windows the app searches the system PATH plus the folders TUIs install into (npm, scoop, winget…).
settings.tuis.path.hint: If a TUI works in your terminal but doesn't show up here, its folder has to be in this list. If you installed it with the app open, try “Search again”; if its folder isn't listed, close and reopen the app so it asks your shell again.
settings.tuis.name: Name
settings.tuis.advancedDesc: None of this is required. Each field you fill in unlocks one more feature: resuming sessions, managing its skills, or showing its history.
settings.tuis.resumeArgsHint: Appended to the command to resume a session. Must include {session}. e.g. --resume {session} or resume {session}. Empty = this TUI always starts fresh.
settings.tuis.skillsDirHint: Relative to the project — where skill symlinks are created. e.g. .agents/skills or .mytui/skills. Empty = the app won't manage its skills.
settings.tuis.sessionsDirHint: Where this TUI stores its sessions. Accepts ~. e.g. ~/.mytui/sessions
settings.tuis.sessionIdFromHint: How to read the id from the session file
settings.orchestrator.desc: When an external agent drives the app through the CLI, every tab it watches sends it events and spends its context. This cap is what keeps it from filling up.
settings.orchestrator.watchLimitHint: Most tabs an orchestrator can follow with «ags watch add» simultaneously.
settings.orchestrator.watchLimitWarning: Past 5 watched tabs, the events alone can fill the model's context before it finishes the task.
settings.skillsDir.desc: Where installed skills are stored globally. Changing it only affects future installs.
settings.skillssh.desc: Searching and installing skills from skills.sh needs nothing installed: the app talks to its API directly. Node.js {{min}} or newer (with npx) is only a fallback, for the few skills skills.sh doesn't have ready to download.
settings.skillssh.firstTime: Checking… the first time npx downloads the CLI, so it can take a while
settings.skillssh.skipped: Not checked: the previous step failed
settings.skillssh.npxMissing: Missing. On Debian and Ubuntu it ships separately from Node (the npm package); nvm includes it
settings.skillssh.searchEmpty: It answered, but with no results
settings.skillssh.fixTitle: Optional: how to install Node.js {{min}} or newer on this system
settings.skillssh.afterInstall: When it finishes, validate again: the app re-reads the PATH, no restart needed.
settings.skillssh.sentToTerminal: It opened in a new terminal in the workspace: close Settings to see it.
accounts.pickHint: The account is fixed now: the TUI reads it at startup, so it can't be changed later. For another account, open another agent.
terminal.accountMissing: This tab's account could not be used ({{error}}). Nothing was launched, to avoid starting with the wrong account.
settings.accounts.pendingLogin: This account still needs a sign-in
settings.accounts.emptyForAgent: You haven't added any account for this TUI yet.
settings.accounts.systemDefault: Your usual account is still there and is used whenever you don't pick one.
settings.accounts.noneInstalled: No installed TUI supports multiple accounts.
settings.accounts.unsupportedNote: Only TUIs that can move their login to another folder are listed. Gemini CLI and Kimi Code expose no way to do that, so giving them multiple accounts would end up with accounts overwriting each other.
settings.accounts.add.title: Add account
settings.accounts.add.name: Account name
settings.accounts.add.nameHelper: This is the folder name {{envVar}} points to. Letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.'
settings.accounts.add.taken: An account with that name already exists for this TUI.
settings.accounts.add.apiKeyHelperClaude: Stored in the system keychain and handed to Claude Code only when this account is launched.
settings.accounts.add.apiKeyHelperCodex: Passed to codex login --with-api-key, which stores it in this account's profile. ADE does not keep it.
settings.accounts.add.baseUrlHelper: For gateways compatible with the Anthropic API, such as OpenRouter. Empty = official API.
settings.accounts.limits.title: Limits for {{name}}
settings.accounts.limits.maxConcurrentHe: Empty = no limit. Tasks beyond it wait their turn; with an automatic account they move to another account with room.
settings.accounts.limits.budgetHelper: Based on the cost the CLI reports (Claude Code, OpenCode). Once reached, the account leaves routing until the spend leaves the 24 h window. Codex does not report cost.
settings.accounts.add.noneInstalled: No installed TUI supports multiple accounts.
settings.accounts.login.title: Sign in to "{{name}}"
settings.accounts.login.helper: This terminal runs "{{command}}" pointed at this account only. Sign in as usual; the app never sees your credentials. Closing it ends the process.
settings.accounts.delete.title: Remove "{{name}}"
settings.accounts.delete.body: You can remove it from the app and keep its files, or also delete the folder holding its login:
settings.cli.desc: Install the ags command to drive the app from your terminal (or from another agent). No administrator permissions needed.
settings.cli.notInPath: That folder isn't in your PATH. If typing ags in a terminal says the command isn't found, add this line to your shell profile:
settings.cli.copyNote: On Windows the executable is copied, so reinstall the CLI after updating the app.
settings.cli.noBinary: No ags binary found next to the app. If you're running in development, build it with: cargo build --bin ags
settings.cli.usage: Try it with: ags app status · ags --help
settings.graphify.desc: Maps the project — code, docs, PDFs, images — into a graph the agent queries instead of reading file by file. Install it once and it shows up as /graphify inside the TUI.
settings.graphify.step.cli.hint: The PyPI package is graphifyy, with two y's, even though the command is graphify. If uv isn't there or pip fails on a managed Python, switch to one of the commands below — or write your own.
settings.graphify.step.skill.hint: Graphify copies its skill into a different folder for each TUI. Pick the destination and the command writes itself; you can keep editing it afterwards.
settings.graphify.sharedDir: ADE AGS mounts its own skills here too. They don't collide: the app only removes the links it put there, and graphify's is a real folder.
settings.graphify.needsCli: Step 2 needs the CLI installed: the skill ships inside it.
settings.graphify.req.desc: Graphify is a Python package, so it needs Python and — to keep the system one clean — uv or pipx. These are the commands from the docs, with your system's already picked.
settings.graphify.req.download: On this system you download it from the official site.
settings.graphify.sentToTerminal: A terminal opened with the command running.
settings.graphify.agentNotReady: That tab has no live terminal yet.
settings.graphify.noAgents: No agent tab is open in this folder.
settings.graphify.group.alwaysOn: Make the assistant always use it
settings.graphify.arg.name: Name
settings.graphify.arg.question: Question
settings.graphify.arg.author: Author
settings.graphify.cmd.extract: Builds the graph. Code is parsed locally with tree-sitter, no LLM; docs, PDFs and images need a backend.
settings.graphify.cmd.update: Re-extracts only what changed. This is what to run after every git pull.
settings.graphify.cmd.check-update: Says whether the graph is stale, without touching it.
settings.graphify.cmd.watch: Keeps the graph current while you work. It never ends on its own.
settings.graphify.cmd.cluster-only: Re-detects communities over the existing graph, without re-extracting.
settings.graphify.cmd.label: Renames the communities with the configured backend.
settings.graphify.cmd.clone: Clones a repo and builds its graph.
settings.graphify.cmd.query: Ask in plain language and get back the subgraph that answers it.
settings.graphify.cmd.path: The shortest path between two things, hop by hop.
settings.graphify.cmd.explain: Everything one node touches, with where each connection came from.
settings.graphify.cmd.export-callflow: Exports the architecture and call flow as HTML with diagrams.
settings.graphify.cmd.hook-install: Rebuilds the graph on every commit and branch switch. Also settles graph.json conflicts.
settings.graphify.cmd.hook-status: Says whether the hooks are in place and point at the right interpreter.
settings.graphify.cmd.prs: Pull request board: CI, reviews, worktrees and graph impact.
settings.graphify.cmd.global-add: Registers this project's graph into the global graph.
settings.graphify.cmd.global-list: The registered projects, with each one's node count.
settings.graphify.cmd.global-remove: Removes a project from the global graph.
settings.graphify.cmd.global-path: Where the global graph file lives.
settings.graphify.cmd.save-result: Records how a question turned out, so the graph learns from what worked.
settings.graphify.cmd.reflect: Aggregates what was recorded into lessons, and flags which nodes became doubtful.
settings.graphify.cmd.serve: Serves the graph as an MCP server, for one agent or the whole team. It never ends on its own.
settings.graphify.cmd.uninstall: Removes it from every platform at once.
settings.graphify.cmd.version: Which version of the package is installed.
settings.graphify.cmd.always-on: Writes that TUI's instruction file (and its hooks, where they exist) so it checks the graph before reading files.
settings.graphify.cmd.always-on-uninstal: Removes those instructions and their hooks.
settings.graphify.cmd.platform-install: Registers the skill by flag, for platforms without their own subcommand.
settings.graphify.cmd.skill-run: Builds the graph from inside the assistant, using its model and its session.
settings.graphify.cmd.skill-add: Fetches a paper, a tweet or a video and adds it to the graph.
settings.graphify.cmd.skill-query: Query the graph from inside the assistant.
settings.graphify.cmd.skill-path: The path between two things, from inside the assistant.
settings.graphify.cmd.skill-explain: Explains a node from inside the assistant.

skills.builder.descriptionPlaceholder: What it does and when to use it

settings.shortcuts.terminalNote: They are handled before the terminal. That is why sections use Ctrl+Shift: the terminal's Ctrl+letter editing keys (Ctrl+E, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H, Ctrl+M) keep working inside agents. The exception is Ctrl+K, which opens the palette; Ctrl+Shift+P does the same.
workspaces.empty: No agents open yet. Open one and its folder shows up here.

marketplace.preview.none: Pick a skill to read it before installing.
marketplace.preview.unavailable: This repository can't serve the skill without installing it, so only the listing data is shown.

skills.palette.searchHint: Type to search the repositories too.
newAgent.title: Open another agent here
newAgent.shellPrelaunchDesc: They run in order before the terminal opens, for example to activate an environment. If you need none, just open it.
skills.preview.none: Pick a skill to see its detail.
accounts.pools.title: Account pools
accounts.pools.hint: Group {{agent}} accounts and let a rule pick one each time. Ask for one as “pool:Name” wherever an account goes (new tab, plan task, Squad).
accounts.pools.order: Order matters for “primary with fallback” and breaks ties in the others.
accounts.pools.strategy.least_used.hint: The one with the most free window right now, among the pool’s accounts only.
accounts.pools.strategy.round_robin.hint: One after another, to spread evenly.
accounts.pools.strategy.sticky.hint: Always the first on the list that can; the next only if it cannot.
accounts.pools.failover.hint: Headless tasks only: after login, model, subscription/credit or usage-limit errors, retry once with another account in the same pool/TUI. Model errors may select an available model from the account catalog. Maximum 1 per task and 3 per pool/hour; 30-minute cooldown. Terminals never switch automatically.
accounts.pools.failover.notice: Task "{{task}}" moved from account {{from}} to {{to}} in pool "{{pool}}" after {{cause}}. Model: {{model}}.
accounts.auto.hint: The one with most quota left

fleet.card.openPaneHint: Pick this same session up in a terminal
fleet.empty.title: No agents in the background

fleet.new.name: Name
fleet.error.noWorkspace: Open a folder before launching an agent.

fleet.rules.empty: No rules yet: agents ask you about everything.
fleet.rules.syntax: Tool or Tool(pattern), with * as a wildcard: Read · Bash(git status*) · Edit(src/**). The first match wins.
fleet.card.takeOverHint: Stops the background agent and continues the same conversation in a terminal
fleet.new.isolateHint: A copy of the repo on a new branch, so it doesn't collide with other agents. Starts from the last commit: uncommitted work isn't there.
fleet.new.isolateNoRepo: Only for folders that are a git repository with at least one commit.
fleet.new.collision: {{n}} agent(s) are already working in this folder. Without a worktree they will edit the same files at once.
fleet.card.rollbackHint: Restores the folder to how it was before this task and queues it again
fleet.rollback.title: Roll back to before this task
fleet.rollback.intro: The folder where “{{title}}” ran goes back to how it was when it started, and the task is queued to run again.
fleet.rollback.noPhoto: {{count}} affected task(s) have no photo (they ran before checkpoints): they are queued again but their folder is not touched.
fleet.rollback.done: {{count}} task(s) were queued again and the folder was restored.
fleet.rollback.noPhotos: No safety photos or manual points in this run yet.
fleet.card.rerouteHint: Stops it and queues it again with a different agent. It keeps its branch and the new agent gets what the previous one did, so it continues from there.
fleet.card.discardHint: Deletes the working copy. Refuses if there are uncommitted changes, and keeps the branch if it has its own commits.
fleet.worktree.discarded: Worktree discarded. Branch {{branch}} had nothing new and was deleted too.
fleet.worktree.discardedKept: Worktree discarded. Branch {{branch}} was kept: it has commits that exist nowhere else.

explorer.delete.bodyFolder: The folder and everything in it go to the system trash, so you can restore them from there.

settings.notifications.label: System notifications
settings.notifications.desc: Notify when a mission finishes or fails, an agent waits for approval or an account has a problem. Only while the app is in the background.
settings.sandbox.label: Agent sandbox
settings.sandbox.desc: Fleet agents only write to their folder, their account and temp files. Credentials for other services are removed from their environment.
settings.sandbox.reason.disabled: Off: agents run with the app permissions
settings.sandbox.reason.missing-bwrap: Install bubblewrap (bwrap) to limit writes. Strict mode blocks tasks until then.
settings.sandbox.reason.missing-sandbox-: sandbox-exec not found: writes are not limited
settings.sandbox.reason.windows: On Windows only process containment and a clean environment apply; writes are not limited. Strict mode blocks tasks.
settings.rendering.gpu.desc: Off keeps text sharp: when WebKitGTK composites the window on the GPU, glyphs come out blurry. Turn it on only if the app feels slow on this machine.
settings.rendering.restart: Takes effect after restarting the app.
settings.rendering.env: The WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE variable in your environment overrides this option.
settings.terminal.gpu.noCompositing: Unavailable: without GPU compositing (Appearance) there is no WebGL, so the terminal is drawn with the DOM.
settings.routing.desc: Which model a fleet agent uses, based on the complexity you pick when launching it. Tried in order: if the first can't be used (not installed, or no account with quota left), it moves on to the next.
settings.routing.lastOne: Each tier needs at least one model
settings.routing.pending: {{agents}}: installed, but it can't run headless yet. Its models will show up here once it can.

browser.debug.network.empty: No requests yet: network traffic is only recorded while this panel is open. Reload the page to see it from the start.
browser.debug.network.name: Name
browser.debug.network.noProxy: No proxy: only requests to other origins are visible
browser.debug.network.headersLimited: From the page you only see the headers the server exposes through CORS (Access-Control-Expose-Headers).
browser.debug.network.noteKept: kept by the preview: never reaches the page
browser.debug.network.websocketBody: What travels over a WebSocket is not recorded.
browser.debug.network.bodyTruncated: Showing the first {{size}}: the full body is {{total}}.
browser.debug.network.bodyTruncatedUnkno: Only the beginning of the body is shown.
browser.debug.network.bodyEvicted: The body is no longer stored: it was released to make room for newer requests.
browser.debug.network.bodyCompressed: The body came compressed ({{encoding}}) and can't be shown.
browser.debug.network.gone: This request is no longer in the log.
browser.debug.network.errorKind.connecti: Connection refused: nothing is listening at that address. Is the server running?
The connection dropped midway: the server crashed or closed it.
browser.debug.network.errorKind.timeout: Timed out: the server didn't answer in time.
browser.debug.network.errorKind.dns: The server name couldn't be resolved (DNS).
browser.debug.network.errorKind.tls: The secure connection (TLS) failed: the certificate is invalid or untrusted.
browser.debug.network.errorKind.protocol: The server answered something that isn't valid HTTP.
browser.debug.network.errorKind.body: The response was cut off while the body was arriving.
browser.debug.network.errorKind.aborted: Cancelled before finishing: a navigation, an AbortController, or the page closed the connection.
browser.debug.network.errorKind.cors: Blocked by CORS: the server doesn't allow the page's origin. The reason is in the console.
browser.debug.network.errorKind.network: No response: the network, a server that is down, or a CORS policy that blocked it. The browser doesn't let the page tell them apart; the console usually says which.
browser.debug.network.code.400: Bad request: the server didn't understand the request (invalid syntax or data).
browser.debug.network.code.401: Unauthenticated: the session or credentials are missing or expired.
browser.debug.network.code.403: Forbidden: the server knows who you are but won't let you access this.
browser.debug.network.code.404: Not found: there's nothing at that path.
browser.debug.network.code.405: Method not allowed: the path exists but doesn't accept this method.
browser.debug.network.code.406: Not acceptable: the server can't respond in the format the Accept header asks for.
browser.debug.network.code.408: The server got tired of waiting for the request.
browser.debug.network.code.409: Conflict with the current state of the resource (for example, a duplicate).
browser.debug.network.code.410: Gone: the resource was permanently removed.
browser.debug.network.code.413: The request body is too large for the server.
browser.debug.network.code.415: Unsupported media type: check the request's Content-Type.
browser.debug.network.code.422: The data is well formed but fails validation.
browser.debug.network.code.429: Too many requests: the server is rate limiting.
browser.debug.network.code.431: The request headers are too large (often because of cookies).
browser.debug.network.code.500: Internal server error: something failed inside, usually an uncaught exception. Check the server logs.
browser.debug.network.code.501: The server doesn't implement this functionality.
browser.debug.network.code.502: Bad gateway: a proxy or gateway got an invalid response from the upstream server.
browser.debug.network.code.503: Service unavailable: the server is down, overloaded, or under maintenance.
browser.debug.network.code.504: The gateway didn't get the upstream server's response in time.
browser.debug.network.code.client: Client error: the request has something the server rejects.
browser.debug.network.code.server: Server error: it failed while processing the request.
browser.debug.storage.hint: What the page stores, per site (address and port). Kept when the app closes, HttpOnly cookies included.
browser.debug.storage.forgetHint: Clears its cookies, localStorage and sessionStorage, including what is saved for the next launch.
browser.debug.storage.notSent: not sent on the last request
browser.debug.perf.live: Measured every {{s}} s while this tab is open.
browser.debug.perf.paintDeferred: It first painted when the tab was shown (it loaded out of view): FCP doesn't measure the load.
browser.debug.perf.vitalsUnavailable: Values shown as — aren't measured by this platform's engine.
browser.debug.perf.memoryUnavailable: This engine (WebKit) doesn't let the page measure its memory. On Windows (WebView2) it shows here; meanwhile, DOM growth is the best hint of a leak.
browser.debug.perf.longTasksUnavailable: This engine doesn't report long tasks (over 50 ms blocking the page).
